repo.name: vllm

detail.body:
## Overview

Cut the gfx942 Kimi-K3 MXFP4-to-int4 MoE requant (`--quantization-config '{"moe":{"weight":"int4_per_group_32"}}'`, added in #51274) from ~19 min to 25 s under pure TP8. TP8 server startup drops from 22.5 min to 3.5 min. The converted weights are byte-identical.


## Validation

**End to end:** 8x MI325X (gfx942), ROCm 10.0, Kimi-K3 with the DSpark draft. The checkpoint was in the page cache for all startup numbers. Before and after use the same base; only `mxfp4.py` differs.

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MLA=1 \
vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 --trust-remote-code --language-model-only -tp 8 [--enable-expert-parallel] \
  --max-model-len 16384 --max-num-seqs 4 --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 \
  --quantization-config '{"moe":{"weight":"int4_per_group_32"}}' \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","model":"Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark","num_speculative_tokens":7,"attention_backend":"TRITON_MLA","draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block"}'
```

| Config | Requant before | Requant after | Startup to `/health` before | Startup to `/health` after | KV cache before | KV cache after |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TP8 | 19 min 15 s | 25 s | 1348 s | 210 s | 27.37 GiB | 28.21 GiB |
| EP8 | 4 min 38 s | 24 s | 431 s | 181 s | 22.57 GiB | 23.41 GiB |

The requant is the time between `Loading weights took` and `Online quantization as part of model loading` on rank 0.

**Accuracy** (GSM8K, 5-shot, `lm_eval --model local-completions`, with the fix):
- TP8: 0.988 ± 0.007 on 250 questions.
- EP8: 1.000 on 100 questions.

The weights are byte-identical to the current code (see below), so I didn't rerun accuracy on the baseline.

**Per-layer microbenchmark:** one full Kimi-K3 MoE layer (w13 + w2), per-rank shapes with `routed_expert_hidden_size` 3584, run under `max_split_size_mb:20` like `gpu_worker.load_model`. Times are the median of 7 runs, alternating before and after. The old code's first run in a fresh process is faster (1.94 s TP8, 0.85 s EP8); its `hipFree` cost grows as the process maps more memory.

| Shape | Time before | Time after | Peak allocated before | after | Peak reserved before | after | `empty_cache()` calls before | after | Byte-identical |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TP8 (896 experts, w13 768 x 3584) | 3.79 s | 0.13 s | 1.56 GiB | 2.89 GiB | 1.85 GiB | 4.56 GiB | 228 | 4 | yes |
| EP8 (112 experts, w13 6144 x 3584) | 3.07 s | 0.30 s | 3.43 GiB | 2.89 GiB | 5.66 GiB | 4.56 GiB | 32 | 4 | yes |

**New test:** `tests/kernels/quantization/test_k3_gfx942_int4_requant.py`. It runs on gfx942 only and is picked up by the existing "(MI300) Quantization Kernels" step. It checks that the output does not depend on chunking, and that no device memory is allocated after the first chunk on the Kimi-K3 TP8 w2 shape under `load_model`'s allocator settings. It passes 4/4 with the fix and fails before it. Against the refactor-only parent (9acd4b58ba), every chunk allocates:

```
E       assert [1724, 1737, ...76, 1789, ...] == [1724, 1724, ...24, 1724, ...]
1 failed, 3 passed
```

Against the first revision of this PR (3bdfe8097f), the shorter last chunk allocates:

```
E       assert [90, 90, 90, 90, 111] == [90, 90, 90, 90, 90]
1 failed, 3 passed
```

For those runs the test loaded `mxfp4.py` from each commit. On the parent I appended `_K3_INT4_CONVERT_CHUNK_VALUES` only so the test's `monkeypatch.setattr` resolves; the old code ignores it.

`tests/models/kimi_k3/test_gfx942_int4.py` and `tests/quantization/test_quantization_config_args.py` still pass.

## Details

**Root cause.** `_setup_kernel_k3_situ_gfx942` converted 8 experts per chunk and called `torch.accelerator.empty_cache()` after every chunk. Pure TP keeps all 896 experts per rank at 1/tp width, so TP8 ran 112 chunks per weight where EP8 runs 14, for the same bytes. That is 20,608 chunks over 92 MoE layers.

Every `empty_cache()` hands the chunk's temporaries back to the driver, and the next chunk allocates them again. In a live TP8 server, a native py-spy profile of the requant showed 92% of the time in `emptyCache -> release_block -> hipFree` (HSA `munmap`/`ioctl`) and about 5% in `hipMalloc`. The conversion kernels themselves barely appeared. That worked out to about 56 ms per chunk.

**Fix.**
- Size each chunk by unpacked values instead of experts, using `_K3_INT4_CONVERT_CHUNK_VALUES = 1 << 27`. TP8 and EP8 both run 19 chunks per w13 and 10 per w2.
- Drop the per-chunk `empty_cache()`, so later chunks reuse the cached temporaries. The cache is still emptied once per converted weight.
- Keep every chunk the same shape by shifting the last chunk back to overlap the previous one. Under `max_split_size_mb:20`, a cached block of 20 MiB or more is only reused for a request less than 20 MiB smaller, so a shorter last chunk would allocate a second set of temporaries. The overlapping experts are recomputed to identical values, which costs less than one chunk per weight.
- The output can't depend on chunk size: `per_1x32_i4_quant`, `shuffle_weight` and `shuffle_scale_for_int4` all work per expert along the leading dimension. The new test checks this explicitly.

**Tradeoffs.** The TP8 per-layer peak grows (allocated 1.56 to 2.89 GiB, reserved 1.85 to 4.56 GiB), because the old TP chunks were tiny. The EP8 peak shrinks (allocated 3.43 to 2.89 GiB, reserved 5.66 to 4.56 GiB). Both stay below the old EP8 peak, which already fit.

---

- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Kimi-K3 gfx942 MXFP4-to-int4 load-time requant."""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+if not current_platform.is_rocm():
+    pytest.skip("requires ROCm", allow_module_level=True)
+
+from vllm.platforms.rocm import on_gfx942  # noqa: E402
+
+if not on_gfx942():
+    pytest.skip("requires gfx942", allow_module_level=True)
+
+pytest.importorskip("aiter")
+
+from aiter.ops.quant import per_1x32_i4_quant  # noqa: E402
+from aiter.ops.shuffle import (  # noqa: E402
+    pack_int8_to_packed_int4,
+    shuffle_scale_for_int4,
+    shuffle_weight,
+)
+from aiter.utility import fp4_utils  # noqa: E402
+
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization import mxfp4  # noqa: E402
+
+NUM_EXPERTS, ROWS, COLS = 128, 256, 2048
+# Kimi-K3 w2 per rank under TP8. 896 experts do not split evenly into chunks.
+TP8_W2_SHAPE = (896, 3584, 384)
+E2M1_VALUES = (0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6, -0.0, -0.5, -1, -1.5, -2, -3, -4, -6)
+
+
+def _mxfp4_experts(
+    num_experts: int = NUM_EXPERTS, rows: int = ROWS, cols: int = COLS
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    gen = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(0)
+    weight = torch.randint(
+        0,
+        256,
+        (num_experts, rows, cols // 2),
+        dtype=torch.uint8,
+        device="cuda",
+        generator=gen,
+    )
+    # Normal E8M0 block scales; 0 and 255 have special meanings.
+    scale = torch.randint(
+        118,
+        132,
+        (num_experts, rows, cols // 32),
+        dtype=torch.uint8,
+        device="cuda",
+        generator=gen,
+    )
+    return weight, scale
+
+
+def _requant(
+    weight: torch.Tensor, scale: torch.Tensor
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    out_weight, out_scale = mxfp4._mxfp4_experts_to_int4_gfx942(
+        torch.nn.Parameter(weight.clone(), requires_grad=False),
+        torch.nn.Parameter(scale.clone(), requires_grad=False),
+    )
+    return out_weight.view(torch.uint8), out_scale.view(torch.uint8)
+
+
+def _reference_requant(
+    weight: torch.Tensor, scale: torch.Tensor
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    """All experts at once, decoding MXFP4 as the OCP MX spec defines it."""
+    num_experts, rows, packed_cols = weight.shape
+    cols = packed_cols * 2
+    # Element 2i is in the low nibble and element 2i + 1 in the high nibble.
+    codes = torch.stack((weight & 0xF, weight >> 4), dim=-1).view(
+        num_experts, rows, cols
+    )
+    values = torch.tensor(E2M1_VALUES, device=weight.device)[codes.long()]
+    block_scales = torch.ldexp(
+        torch.ones_like(scale, dtype=torch.float32), scale.int() - 127
+    )
+    weight_bf16 = (
+        (values.view(num_experts, rows, cols // 32, 32) * block_scales.unsqueeze(-1))
+        .view(num_experts, rows, cols)
+        .to(torch.bfloat16)
+    )
+
+    weight_int4, weight_scale = per_1x32_i4_quant(weight_bf16)
+    packed = pack_int8_to_packed_int4(shuffle_weight(weight_int4, (16, 16)))
+    packed_scale = shuffle_scale_for_int4(weight_scale, group_size=32).reshape(-1)
+    return (
+        packed.view(torch.uint8).view(num_experts, rows, packed_cols),
+        packed_scale.view(torch.uint8),
+    )
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def load_model_allocator_settings():
+    original = torch._C._accelerator_getAllocatorSettings()
+    prefix = original.strip().rstrip(",")
+    settings = "max_split_size_mb:20"
+    torch._C._accelerator_setAllocatorSettings(
+        f"{prefix},{settings}" if prefix else settings
+    )
+    yield
+    torch._C._accelerator_setAllocatorSettings(original)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "experts_per_chunk",
+    [1, 5, NUM_EXPERTS],
+    ids=["one_expert", "uneven_last_chunk", "single_chunk"],
+)
+def test_requant_matches_reference(monkeypatch, experts_per_chunk):
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        mxfp4, "_K3_INT4_CONVERT_CHUNK_VALUES", experts_per_chunk * ROWS * COLS
+    )
+    weight, scale = _mxfp4_experts()
+
+    out_weight, out_scale = _requant(weight, scale)
+    ref_weight, ref_scale = _reference_requant(weight, scale)
+
+    assert torch.equal(out_weight, ref_weight)
+    assert torch.equal(out_scale, ref_scale)
+
+
+def test_requant_allocates_device_memory_only_in_first_chunk(
+    monkeypatch, load_model_allocator_settings
+):
+    """Later chunks, the last one included, must reuse the first chunk's cached
+    blocks under load_model's allocator settings."""
+    weight, scale = _mxfp4_experts(*TP8_W2_SHAPE)
+    _requant(weight, scale)
+    torch.accelerator.empty_cache()
+
+    device_allocs = []
+    mxfp4_to_f32 = fp4_utils.mxfp4_to_f32
+
+    def recording_mxfp4_to_f32(x):
+        device_allocs.append(torch.accelerator.memory_stats()["num_device_alloc"])
+        return mxfp4_to_f32(x)
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(fp4_utils, "mxfp4_to_f32", recording_mxfp4_to_f32)
+    _requant(weight, scale)
+    device_allocs.append(torch.accelerator.memory_stats()["num_device_alloc"])
+
+    assert len(device_allocs) > 3
+    assert device_allocs[1:] == [device_allocs[1]] * (len(device_allocs) - 1)

+# The gfx942 int4 requant unpacks MXFP4 to f32 and peaks above 20 GiB per rank
+# if all experts convert at once, so it converts in chunks. Chunks are sized by
+# unpacked values rather than experts so that pure TP, which holds every expert
+# at 1/tp width, runs as many chunks as EP.
+_K3_INT4_CONVERT_CHUNK_VALUES = 1 << 27
+
+
+def _mxfp4_experts_to_int4_gfx942(
+    weight: torch.nn.Parameter,
+    scale: torch.nn.Parameter,
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    """Requantize packed MXFP4 experts to shuffled groupwise int4 for gfx942.
+
+    Takes ``(E, N, K // 2)`` MXFP4 weights with ``(E, N, K // 32)`` E8M0
+    scales and returns ``(E, N, K // 2)`` packed int4 with flattened
+    per-32 scales.
+    """
+    from aiter import dtypes as aiter_dtypes
+    from aiter.ops.quant import per_1x32_i4_quant
+    from aiter.ops.shuffle import (
+        pack_int8_to_packed_int4,
+        shuffle_scale_for_int4,
+        shuffle_weight,
+    )
+    from aiter.utility import fp4_utils
+
+    fp4_dtype = torch.float4_e2m1fn_x2
+    e8m0_dtype = torch.float8_e8m0fnu
+
+    w_all = weight.data.view(fp4_dtype)
+    s_all = scale.data.view(e8m0_dtype)
+    num_experts, rows, packed_cols = w_all.shape
+    chunk = min(
+        num_experts,
+        max(1, _K3_INT4_CONVERT_CHUNK_VALUES // (rows * packed_cols * 2)),
+    )
+
+    # Write chunks into a preallocated output. torch.cat of a list
+    # would hold the full result twice at the join.
+    out_packed: torch.Tensor | None = None
+    out_scale: torch.Tensor | None = None
+    scale_stride = 0
+    for lo in range(0, num_experts, chunk):
+        # Shift the last chunk back so every chunk has the same shapes. Under
+        # load_model's max_split_size_mb, a shorter chunk cannot reuse the
+        # cached blocks. The overlapping experts are recomputed identically.
+        lo = min(lo, num_experts - chunk)
+        hi = lo + chunk
+        weight_f32 = fp4_utils.mxfp4_to_f32(w_all[lo:hi])
+        scale_f32 = fp4_utils.e8m0_to_f32(s_all[lo:hi])
+        chunk_experts, output_size, input_size = weight_f32.shape
+        weight_bf16 = (
+            (
+                weight_f32.view(chunk_experts, output_size, input_size // 32, 32)
+                * scale_f32.view(chunk_experts, output_size, input_size // 32, 1)
+            )
+            .view(chunk_experts, output_size, input_size)
+            .to(torch.bfloat16)
+        )
+        del weight_f32, scale_f32
+
+        weight_int4, weight_scale = per_1x32_i4_quant(weight_bf16)
+        del weight_bf16
+        weight_int4 = weight_int4.view(aiter_dtypes.i4x2).view(
+            chunk_experts, output_size, input_size
+        )
+        weight_packed = pack_int8_to_packed_int4(
+            shuffle_weight(weight_int4.view(aiter_dtypes.i8), (16, 16))
+        )
+        del weight_int4
+        chunk_packed = weight_packed.view(
+            chunk_experts, output_size, input_size // 2
+        ).view(aiter_dtypes.i4x2)
+        chunk_scale = (
+            shuffle_scale_for_int4(weight_scale, group_size=32).view(-1).contiguous()
+        )
+        if out_packed is None:
+            out_packed = torch.empty(
+                (num_experts,) + tuple(chunk_packed.shape[1:]),
+                dtype=chunk_packed.dtype,
+                device=chunk_packed.device,
+            )
+            scale_stride = chunk_scale.numel() // chunk_experts
+            out_scale = torch.empty(
+                num_experts * scale_stride,
+                dtype=chunk_scale.dtype,
+                device=chunk_scale.device,
+            )
+        assert out_packed is not None
+        assert out_scale is not None
+        out_packed[lo:hi].copy_(chunk_packed)
+        out_scale[lo * scale_stride : hi * scale_stride].copy_(chunk_scale)
+        # No empty_cache() here: the next chunk reuses these cached
+        # blocks, while releasing them costs a hipFree per temporary.
+        del weight_packed, weight_scale, chunk_packed, chunk_scale
+
+    del w_all, s_all
+    assert out_packed is not None
+    assert out_scale is not None
+    return out_packed, out_scale
+
+
 def _use_k3_situ_int4_gfx942(moe: FusedMoEConfig) -> bool:
     """Opt-in gfx942 MXFP4-to-int4 requant for Kimi-K3 SiTU experts."""
     from vllm.platforms import current_platform

The conversion is also faster than at 2^28 (TP8 0.13 s vs 0.27 s per layer, EP8 0.30 s vs 0.55 s).

Yes, confirmed! At production shapes the first chunk made 20 device allocations, middle chunks 0, and the last, shorter chunk 5 to 21 more, held next to the cached full-size set.

Fixed now by shifting the last chunk back so it overlaps the previous one, so every chunk has the same shapes. The overlapping experts are recomputed to identical values, which costs less than one chunk per weight. Now no chunk after the first allocates device memory, and the new test checks that.

Alternatives I measured: calling `empty_cache()` before the short chunk fixes the peak but keeps an extra round of allocations and frees; balancing chunk sizes still leaves sizes one expert apart (about 88 MB of f32 under EP8), which still misses; preallocating the outputs before the loop added an allocation per chunk.

End to end with this revision: TP8 requant 25 s (was 59 s), startup 210 s (was 235 s); EP8 requant 24 s (was 63 s), startup 181 s (was 216 s). GSM8K 5-shot TP8 0.988 (250 questions), EP8 1.000 (100).

inline_comments.body:
Agreed, the chunking self-comparison was the weak one: it compared the helper with itself, so a bug that's the same in every chunk would pass. In 357c535 I replaced it with `test_requant_matches_reference`, which compares against an unchunked reference. The reference decodes MXFP4 straight from the OCP MX spec and applies aiter's int4 quant and shuffles to all experts at once. The shuffles come from aiter because the layout is whatever aiter's kernel expects.

To check that it catches bugs, I also injected a dropped block scale and a swapped nibble order into the helper. The old test passed both, and the new one fails both. It also passes on the pre-PR code, so the reference matches the original implementation.

I'd keep the allocation test, though. The bug this PR fixes doesn't change outputs: a per-chunk `empty_cache()` or a short last chunk would keep the bytes identical and only slow startup (TP8 requant 19 min vs 25 s). The allocation test is the only check for that, and it takes about a second. Happy to drop it if you feel strongly about it, just let me know. 

Keeping a good balance of needed and redundant tests is always hard :)

Checked: no change needed. 

The existing `:amd: (MI300) Quantization Kernels` step in `.buildkite/test-amd.yaml` (and its mirror in `.buildkite/test_areas/kernels.yaml`) runs `pytest kernels/quantization` on MI300 (gfx942), and both `vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization` and `tests/kernels/quantization` are in its `source_file_dependencies`. 

In [build #98073](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/98073) all four tests in the file ran on the MI300 shards and passed. The MI355 step collects it too but skips it, since the test is gfx942-only.
